Questions you may have.desc: Nix is the package manager that NixOS is built upon. It replaces standard package management tools (such as apt, pacman, dpkg, snap) and builds your packages in isolation under /nix/store. Nothing is written to /usr/bin or /lib. In the case of NixOS the whole machine (kernel, services and dotfiles) is one expression evaluate from something called a flake. This is declared and rebuilt on a repo under sudo privileges, which means every change is atomic and easily reversible. It helps us easily manage Codeship's workstations and quickly make changes to all of them

Questions you may have.cmd: How do I install packages then?
Questions you may have.desc: Most of the time you don't even need to edit the flake! in NixOS, the habit of using 'sudo apt install' to download and run binaries is replaced with three other possibilities: 'nix shell' - for one terminal session, 'nix run' - for one command, 'nix develop' - for a project and all its dependencies. Reach for help if you want to propose globally installed packages for the lab ;)

Questions you may have.cmd: Can I use my other standard linux commands?
Questions you may have.desc: Yes - coreutils, bash, systemd, git, ssh, journalctl and pipes work as expected
